core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 1542-1543): it follows directly from the comparison of sheaf conditions under tautological equivalence together with the definitions.

Part (2) (proof lines 1546-1556): given a sheaf for the second site and a covering of the first, the author chooses a refinement in the second site and observes that the sheaf condition holds both for that refinement and for the induced coverings of the members, whence the sheaf condition for the given covering follows from the comparison result.
proof_roadmap: Use the comparison of sheaf conditions for tautological equivalence in part (1).
For part (2), choose a refinement in the second site.
Apply the refinement comparison to obtain the sheaf condition for the first site.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares the categories of sheaves of two sites on the same category: if every covering of the first is tautologically equivalent to one of the second then the sheaves of the second are sheaves for the first, and similarly for refinements, with equality when the comparison holds in both directions (statement lines 1515-1539). The proof is short but complete: part (1) follows directly from the comparison of sheaf conditions under tautological equivalence (proof lines 1542-1543); for part (2) the author chooses a refinement of a given covering in the second site and observes that the sheaf condition holds for that refinement and for the induced coverings, so that the comparison result gives the sheaf condition for the given covering (proof lines 1546-1556). The non-formal content is the choice of refinement and the application of the comparison. The claim is H1: two short arguments, each written out.
